title.label: Great except for bizarre sync issues

content.label:
Overall a great idea and well executed except for the iCloud sync behavior. It's honestly beyond me how the sync in this app works. I'll often complete a task and then it will immediately uncomplete itself and the maybe come back shortly after. This should never happen if sync was implemented in a sane way, where each device records immutable events with timestamps and you just apply them in order. Once I've completed a task that event should be recorded and I should never see a state where the task is not complete unless I explicitly undo the completion (which itself is another event and applied in the right order based on timestamps should not cause any problems). But I constantly get into states where tasks I completed on the current device mysteriously show up as not completed anymore and maybe correct themselves later. Or not.

I use this app across iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch which makes the sync issues rather obnoxious. It does seem like it's gotten "better" but this isn't something that should get incrementally better, they should just fix their sync design and all the issues would go away permanently.

title.label: It Knows You Better Than You Think You Know Yourself

content.label:
This is the habit tracker you need even if it doesn't seem like the one you think you need.

As someone with ADHD turning mundane tasks into dopamine-producing rewards is paramount (if I hope to function as an adult anyway). I've used Notion, Habitify, and Habitica for weeks and months at a time and always come back to Streaks. Although Streaks is not objectively the most robust or feature-rich solution, that's exactly why it's the best - especially the 24 habit cap. For me I would enevitably end up creating more habits than I could realistically accomplish each day with the other apps. But with Streaks they forced me to think more critically on the most important 24 habits I wanted to form a streak with. I've found that actually being able to complete your habits is FAR more motivating than simply having every concievable habit in your app. And finally, dividing the 24 habits into four pages might seem awkward at first but it turns out that by segmenting your day into four sections it's actaully more exciting and motivating to complete each page thus giving you more sustained motivation throughout the day - who knew!? All that being said the app is top-notch quality and the fact that I can use on my mac, phone, and watch really does make this the best habit tracking app....for apple users!

I've used this app for years. I bought the lifetime membership almost immediately. But recent changes have me debating leaving the app. 

It used to be that if you paused tasks you didn't lose your streak. Now though, pausing tasks only makes it so the app stops bothering you. I lose all my streaks every time I unpause. Sometimes my tasks aren't physically possible for me because of life circumstances. I've searched the settings several times and can't find a way to return it to what it used to be. 

I liked this app BECAUSE I could pause things and not lose my streak. It's one of the few apps that did that. But without it, I might as well go back to tracking my habits in excel and setting manual reminders.
Love the app—it’s to the point and very affordable, but I can’t bear its icon color!!!

title.label: Transformative & Seamless: Streaks - A Cornerstone of My Fitness Journey

content.label:
As someone deeply invested in fitness and technology, I'm often on the lookout for apps that not only promise results but actually deliver them. Streaks is one such gem. It has been an integral part of my daily routine, contributing significantly to my achievement of a 1,368-day workout streak. This journey of mine even caught the attention of Men's Health, a testament to the efficacy of the habits Streaks helped me cultivate.

What sets Streaks apart is its simplicity and focus. It's not just another task manager; it's a lifestyle enhancer. The app's intuitive design, available on both iPhone and Apple Watch, makes tracking daily goals effortless and engaging. Its ability to sync seamlessly with Apple Health is a game-changer. This integration means that data from various workouts and health apps I use are automatically imported into Streaks. Why is this important? It provides a holistic view of my fitness regimen without the hassle of manual entries. The convenience of having all my health data consolidated in one place cannot be overstated. It allows for a more comprehensive understanding of my fitness progress and patterns.

Another aspect worth noting is how Streaks leverages the psychology of habit formation. The app doesn't just track your habits; it encourages and motivates you to maintain them. The satisfaction of maintaining a streak is a powerful motivator, and Streaks capitalizes on this brilliantly. For me, seeing my workout streak grow day by day was not just motivational but also a source of personal pride.

I first stumbled upon Streaks through a blog post by Matt Mullenweg, founder and CEO of Automattic/WordPress. His recommendation spoke volumes, and the app has lived up to every bit of the promise. Whether you're looking to start a new habit or maintain an existing one, Streaks is the perfect companion.

Streaks stands out as one of the most useful apps on my iPhone and Apple Watch. It is more than just an app; it is a daily partner in my journey towards sustained health and wellness. For anyone looking to embark on or maintain a health journey, I cannot recommend Streaks highly enough. It is a prime example of how technology can be harnessed to improve our daily lives in meaningful ways.

title.label: Life-changing but with a lot more room for improvement

content.label:
I started using Streaks as a part of my depression combating plan. I needed an app to remind me of the basics of life such as taking a shower, taking vitamins and meds, housekeeping, tracking weight, working out, sleeping on time, drinking water, brushing teeth, enjoying a cup of coffee, reading a book, writing a journal, ..., etc.
It has dramatically changed my life in just a couple of weeks. I don't really care about doing streaks, but I desperately needed reminders and a way to keep track of things.

== What I Like ==
- Integrates well with iOS, WatchOS, MacOS, Apple Health, Apple Shortcuts, and widgets
- You can connect "start actions" to Apple shortcuts, which I absolutely love, since I turn related "Focus" modes on (but I can't turn it off, see below)
- It allows you to export your data as CSV
- Many options for theming

== Needs Improvement ==
- The UI/UX is an absolute nightmare. It's not intuitive at all. You find what you're looking for if you're lucky. There are surprising elements, random icons, and random numbers all over the place and you have to press everything randomly like a monkey to discover features. It's like they forced themselves to be in a certain visual language/framework, and they lost all sense of common sense. I had (and sometimes still have) a very hard time understanding why I have different sections, what is the icon on top for, how to reorder things when labels are not visible, why does some tasks don't allow me to change the task type and some other properties, what does it mean when I set my Task Days to 1 day a week, and there's a setting right below saying 1 time/day? What does the numbers at the bottom mean? Why is the stats icon a star, which commonly means "favorite" in the industry? What does "upcoming" task even mean, I have 24 habits and I they don't need to follow a specific order, I just need to make sure I do them. The litmus test for good design is "do they need a manual for this"? And you ABSOLUTELY need the manual for more than half of the features.
- Stats are only limited to the page you're viewing, I need an overall view (again, why do we have pages?). Also you can't view the actual values on the graph, which renders them useless, you're just looking at random bumps... What does the "time graph" even mean? Is it an average of every day? 
- Limits you to only a maximum of 24 habits. I already filled it up and can't add more...
- App timers are not syncing across devices unless you stop it on one and refresh it on the other, and sometimes it doesn't work at all
- You can't connect a shortcut to a "timer stopped" action for timers. This is really bad because I can't turn off my Focus mode automatically when the timer is done
- When you connect a shortcut, it opens the Shortcuts App every time the action is triggered, which is really annoying
- Multiple timers can be started together, which is pretty bad since I want other timers to stop when I start a different timer. Sometimes I forget to stop the other timers and it skews the data
- Data exports don't contain your Apple Health stats
- There's no RPC APIs (just callback URLs) I can use to integrate my habits or stats with my Obsidian notes

Pretty sure I forgot many other annoyances I have, but all these improvements are listed simply because I love the app and I can see the potential if the gaps are filled. Many thanks to all the people involved in making this app, and I truly hope to see the app in a better place soon.

3. This one isn’t that important but I believe that adding a checklist function to this app for different task you make would be absolutely insane. It would definitely change the game for me.

All in all this a great app and it will help you.

title.label: CHANGED MY LIFE IN 40 DAYS - MUST HAVE APP

content.label:
I have been wanting an app like this for years. A fellow self help junkie friend of mine told me about this app & at first I was reticent to want to buy it, but I trusted him so I did & wow! Best $4.99 I may have ever spent! 

I am not 40+ days into using it & I have limited my social media to 30 minutes to 1 hour a day, I’m more productive & focused for sure, I have started writing my book & I’m tracking my writing progress, and I have gotten several other people to get the app as well. I finally have the right tool that’s fun & easy to use to keep me on track with my own goals! 

I have tried other free habits apps & there is nothing like Streaks out there. This is literally a dreams come true. I only wish there was a goals at a glance page for my 6 daily goals, 90 day goals, my monthly goals, & my yearly goals. Maybe they can make that next! I also wish I could have 6 more streaks goals. I feel like I need 1 more page or at least an option for more pages. Not because I do every streak goal every day, but seeing my overall goals everyday keeps me motivated and focused! 

I separated my streaks pages into 4 categories: 

Page 1: My Morning Routine (Bible, prayer, write my ten 90 day goals, read 10 pages or 20 minutes, write my 6 goals for the day..) 
Page 2: My Health / Day Routine including listening to motivational audio (often while I work out), 72 oz water, get ready for the day) 
Page 3: My Work Habits (work 30 min on my business, Read 30 min to 1 hour in my industry to join the top 10%, plan, film or edit a YouTube video..) 
Page 4: My night routine (putting the kitchen to bed, checking screen time to see if I made my 30 min - 1 hour social media goal, clean my face, bedtime..) 

Thank you Streaks! I hope this doesn’t become a subscription because currently it’s the best thing ever. I will be making a YouTube video about this app at YouTube.com/CamilleHarris
